title: Dashboard role kits and trace annotation playbook
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact playbook for building role-focused mini-dashboard kits and a lean trace-annotation cheat-sheet for oncall and product stakeholders. Goal: reduce time-to-insight for three personas (SRE/operator, Product PM, Exec) while keeping trace volume and query cost bounded.

Context and problem we see:
- Too many dashboards, overlapping metrics; oncall can’t find the single-pane view for a regression.
- Product owners ask for UX-latency + hallucination signals but don’t have a repeatable mapping to traces.
- Traces are noisy: inconsistent span names, missing user/session tags, variable sampling.

Principles (short):
- One front-line view per persona (operator, product, exec) with strict widget budgets (3-6 widgets).
- Metric source + owner annotated on every widget.
- Trace anchors for each widget: clear link from widget to 1-3 representative spans.
- Cost-awareness: default sampling + synthetic probes to act as smoke checks.

Role kits (templates):
1) Operator (SRE) kit - "Fast triage"
  - Widgets (priority order): 1) Request rate & error rate (5m/1h), 2) P50/P95 TTF token & TTF model-serving, 3) KV cache hit ratio, 4) Inflight queue depth, 5) Tail latency heatmap (quantile buckets)
  - Acceptance criteria: can determine within 3 minutes whether issue is capacity, cache, model slow-path, or network.
  - Trace anchor: span name pattern: serving.request -> runtime.kv.prefetch -> model.infer.encode -> model.infer.decode. Link to trace sample query with session id.

2) Product kit - "Quality & UX"
  - Widgets: 1) perceived latency by user cohort, 2) hallucination-rate (sampled human-labeled) trend, 3) quality-regression alerts (eval set pass rate), 4) cost-per-conversion
  - Acceptance criteria: product can detect a quality regression vs baseline and identify candidate model or prompt causes.
  - Trace anchor: user-session span enrichment (user_cohort, prompt_version). Capture top-k tokens count and function-call durations.

3) Executive kit - "Health snapshot"
  - Widgets: 1) Overall availability (SLA), 2) Avg 95th latency, 3) Cost burn vs forecast, 4) Major active incidents count
  - Acceptance criteria: 1-slide visibility for weekly exec sync.

Metric definitions (canonical samples):
- request.rate: count(api.request) / minute, tag: model, route, tenant
- request.error_rate: count(api.request where status >=500) / count(api.request) (1h rolling)
- ttf.token.p50/p95: time from request received -> first token emitted per request
- model.infer.duration: model execution time (kernel start->kernel end) p50/p95
- kv.cache.hit_ratio: hits/(hits+misses) over 15m
Notes: every metric must have owner in metric catalog (owner@example.com).

Tracing conventions (cheat-sheet):
- Top-level span naming: <service>.<operation> (lowercase, hyphens) e.g., serving.request, model.infer
- Child spans: include suffix with role: runtime.kv.prefetch, runtime.kv.evict, http.downstream.call
- Mandatory tags on root span: request_id, tenant_id, model_name, route, prompt_version, user_cohort (if applicable), sample_reason (if sampled)
- Trace sampling: baseline 1% for production, 10% for requests with error status >=500, 100% for synthetic canaries and failing requests in last 1h window bucket
- Span payload clipping: drop prompt text by default; store prompt hash + truncated first 512 chars for triage only

Dashboard wiring & trace link pattern:
- Each interactive widget must include a trace-link that injects time window + a small filter expression (e.g., request_id=%s OR tenant=%s) and the anchor span name. Use short trace snippets for quick preview (top 3 spans).

Sampling & cost control knobs:
- Low cost sample: take sparse pre-sampled traces for baseline metrics (1%); escalate sampling when a spike threshold on metrics is crossed.
- Retention tiers: high-fidelity traces for 7 days, compact metadata for 90 days.

Design doc checklist for new dashboards (ticks):
- [ ] Owner assigned and listed on widget footer
- [ ] Persona targeted and 3 key questions answered by the kit
- [ ] Trace anchors defined for top widgets (span patterns + example query)
- [ ] Sampling policy and cost estimate included
- [ ] Linked eval prompt set for product quality widgets

Operational runbook snippets:
- If P95 latency doubles and request.rate unchanged -> check KV cache hit ratio + model.infer.duration p95. Link to trace samples with runtime.kv.prefetch spans.
- If hallucination-rate jumps -> pull eval prompt set diffs and linked traces where prompt_version differs. Check model variant rollouts.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- How do we standardize human-labeled "hallucination-rate" signal across CS teams? (work with CS to define minimal labeling rubric)
- Should product kits include a "replayable prompt" widget to re-run requests against canary model? Security implications TBD.

Next steps & owners:
- Ethan: prototype Operator kit in Grafana using compact panels (ETA 2 weeks) - JIRA: OBS-410
- Ava: trace annotation linter (enforce mandatory tags) - PR draft in telemetry repo
- Priya: metric catalog entries for the 12 canonical metrics in this doc (ETA end of month)

Notes to self / roughs:
- Keep panels narrow; default time windows should be 5m/1h/24h depending on persona.
- Consider small "mini-trace viewer" embedded in panel for top 3 spans only to avoid heavy query cost.

References: link to existing probe list + canary patterns in Confluence (see linked_artifacts).
